item.title: Permafrost thaws worldwide as active layers deepen from 2000 to 2024
item.description: An international study led by researchers at the George Washington University indicates clear global evidence that permafrost is thawing across much of the planet. Using more than two decades of field observations from 156 monitoring sites across the Arctic, Antarctic and high-mountain regions, the study found increases in the thickness of the active layer, the uppermost layer above permafrost that thaws and refreezes each year. The findings confirm that permafrost degradation accelerated globally between 2000 and 2024. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Liquid gallium experiment confirms key flow regime inside rapidly rotating stars and planets
item.description: Since we cannot look into the interiors of stars and planets, we rely on lab experiments to replicate the physical processes that occur there. Led by the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA), an international research team has produced the first experimental verification of a theoretically predicted flow state deemed characteristic of the interiors of rapidly rotating celestial bodies. The Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR) also participated in the study, which has been published in Physical Review Letters. item.title: For nearly a decade, a California town fought to seize its privately owned water utility
item.description: In a landmark decision, California's Supreme Court dismissed a town's claim regarding the use of eminent domain for utility purposes. The judges emphasized the need for a thorough, independent evaluation of necessity declarations before any utility can be seized. This shift significantly impacts how courts will weigh municipal efforts to take over private utility companies, allowing private water, gas, and electricity firms to challenge such actions more effectively. item.title: Más sanciones contra Irán: ¿podrá Trump impedir que China siga haciendo negocios con Teherán?
item.description: Donald Trump busca endurecer el cerco económico sobre Irán mientras la guerra con la República Islámica permanece estancada. Washington apuesta por nuevas sanciones para “asfixiar” a Teherán, pero se enfrenta a un obstáculo clave: China es el principal comprador del petróleo iraní. Antes del conflicto, adquiría cerca del 80% del crudo que Irán vendía al exterior. ¿Hasta dónde puede llegar la presión de Trump y podrá impedir que China siga comercializando con Irán? ¿Qué consecuencias pueden tener estas sanciones? Lo analizamos con Raffaele Mauriello en Expreso de Oriente. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
